label: D2 after a rewarded a2 -> common S2 repeat (mid-episode)
explanation: Fires only at D2 (100% of mass), only when the agent chose a2 and reached S2 by a common transition (in_action=2, in_state=2: zero activity on S1 or rare transitions), and only when the previous trial was rewarded (prev_reward=1) and was also an a2 choice (stay on a2). All variables are observed at D2. It is also strongly gated by episode time: silent in trials 0-9, weak in 10-19, near-silent in 90-99; restricting to trials 20-89 raises dev F1 from 0.80 to 0.90, so the predicate includes that window (ep_trial is not a task input but the agent can track elapsed time in its state). Without the time gate the predicate keeps recall ~1.0 but precision 0.67. Magnitude grows along a streak of consecutive rewarded a2->S2c trials in the example windows (e.g. 0.26 -> 0.36 over successive trials) and is higher when model value is high (top value bin rate 21%); it is asymmetric: no counterpart for a1->S1. Remaining false positives are mostly a2->S2c steps right after a break in the streak (e.g. after an unrewarded or rare trial earlier) or early/late in the episode.

issues: The checkable claims hold. On the dev split, activity occurs only at D2: D1 and GO have 0 active steps, and D2 holds 100% of the mass. All of it is on a2 -> S2 common trials: S1 has 0 active steps and rare transitions have 0. prev_reward==0 has only 54 active steps out of 58395. The ep_trial gating is real: trials 0-9 have precision 0.0, 10-19 have 0.09 and 90-99 have 0.0006. The reported test scores reproduce exactly: P 0.818, R 0.982, F1 0.893.

There is a systematic false-positive class the explanation leaves out: the previous a2 trial had a RARE transition (a2 -> S1, rewarded). Inside the original predicate, adding prev_common==0 gives precision 0.37 with recall 0.042, on 6719 predicted steps. That is about 4200 false positives, roughly a third of all false positives. Adding prev_common!=0 instead gives precision 0.88 with recall 0.94. Without the episode-time limit, a previous a2 rare-rewarded trial gives precision 0.27. So the unit needs a run of common-rewarded a2 -> S2 trials, not just 'previous trial a2 and rewarded'. The explanation's own remark about false positives 'soon after a break in the run' partly points to this but never names it.

The upper episode-time cutoff sits a little early. With the other conditions held, precision is 0.73 at trial 85, 0.40 at 87, 0.16 at 88 and 0.03 at 89, so a cutoff at < 88 fits better than < 90. The lower bound of 20 is about right (precision 0.56 at trial 20, 0.22 at 18).

Smaller remaining pattern: when the hidden good state is S1, precision drops to 0.67 on 2729 steps. These are mostly runs of a2 -> S2 reward just after a reversal. The class is small and fits the agent tracking the observed reward run, so it is not used in the predicate.
The predicate uses no future variable, and none of the added terms are future variables either (prev_common is observed at D2).
